items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Spikes Brothers' only in the context of a venue owner/manager mentioned by the interviewer, with no personal interaction or relationship described by the interviewee.

ctx.x: But they were promoters too. They had the dreamland. Yeah. They ran the dreamland.

Yeah. They bought it from some other guy after we went, what is the place where we played? Cadillac. Cadillac. The guy sold it to Spikes Brothers and we went back and went for Spikes Brothers. Manly come down and started us off and he left. Oh, my mother was there. Yeah. Well, you stayed, you couldn't stay.
Yeah. Well, were they connected with the Spikes Brothers circus at all? Those Spikes Brothers? No. Different people out there.

items.title: Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1957-04-20
items.q: And then they asked me to record for them... I went down and record for them.

ctx.x: You mean with that? For the Spikes Brothers. And the Nordscocks. You do to us.

Oh, after I started playing, I told you, I sent you for my band. Yeah. And I got a Spikes Brothers. The book was the saxophone play, you know. Yeah. One play to take home. And so they opened a music store in Los Angeles. And then they asked me to record for them. Where were you? Well, when they asked me to record, I was here in Oakland. I was working in Oakland at Creole Cafe in Ferdinand Wood. And so I went down on, after engaging with them, I went down. No, I made a special trick. Go down and record for them.
You took the whole band with you? Mm-hmm. Went on the train?
